en.title: Fallout 5 Officially Confirmed in Pre-Production After Elder Scrolls 6
en.summary: Bethesda Game Studios has officially confirmed that Fallout 5 is in pre-production, though it will follow the highly anticipated The Elder Scrolls 6. This news comes amidst broader discussions about the studio's development pipeline and the impact of recent industry shifts.
en.body:
The wasteland beckons once more, but patience is a virtue for any true Fallout fan. Bethesda Game Studios has confirmed that **Fallout 5** is officially in pre-production. However, this isn't a case of immediate Reclamation Day; the next installment in the beloved post-apocalyptic RPG series will launch *after* **The Elder Scrolls 6**. This strategic prioritization means that while **Fallout 5** is on the drawing board, **The Elder Scrolls 6** remains Bethesda's top development focus.

This confirmation arrives as Bethesda navigates a dynamic industry landscape. Studio director **Todd Howard** has shed light on the studio's roadmap, emphasizing that both **The Elder Scrolls VI** and **Fallout 5** are being developed using **Creation Engine 3**. This shared technology platform, built since the launch of **Starfield**, is designed to allow teams to support multiple projects simultaneously, potentially streamlining development for future titles. While the exact scope and direction of **Fallout 5** may still be influenced by recent industry shifts, its existence in the development pipeline is now a certainty.

## A Future Built on Creation Engine 3

The development of **Fallout 5** alongside **The Elder Scrolls 6** on the same engine signals a commitment to leveraging existing technology. **Creation Engine 3** aims to provide a unified foundation, allowing for greater efficiency and potentially more consistent experiences across Bethesda's flagship franchises. This approach means that the teams won't need to reinvent the wheel for each new project, which could be crucial for managing the long development cycles typical of these massive RPGs. The news also fuels speculation about other potential Fallout projects, with reports suggesting that Bethesda and external studios like **Obsidian Entertainment** might be exploring further expansions within the franchise.

## The Long Wait and Fan Anticipation

For fans eager to return to the irradiated ruins, the confirmed order of development means a significant wait. **The Elder Scrolls 6** has no firm release year yet, and **Fallout 5** will follow that. While some reports have tentatively placed **Fallout 5** around 2025-2027, Bethesda has not provided any official release window. The long gaps between major releases are a hallmark of Bethesda's ambitious development, but they also foster immense anticipation. The community is abuzz with theories about potential settings, gameplay innovations, and how the narrative might tie into the recently released Amazon TV series, which **Todd Howard** has indicated will influence the game's world. The overarching sentiment is one of hopeful patience, understanding that a game of this scale requires time and dedication.

## What's Next

Details regarding **Fallout 5**'s release date, setting specifics, and gameplay features have not yet been announced. Players will need to keep a close eye on future Bethesda showcases and **Xbox Games Showcase** events for any further updates, with **The Elder Scrolls 6** expected to be the primary focus for the foreseeable future.

content_raw: Bethesda's gone and done it again. It's reconfirmed that Fallout 5 is in development even though it's still years away from Reclamation Day. As we once knew about the next Elder Scrolls' place in the development pipes relative to Starfield, Fallout 5 will launch after TES6, and this time we've not even got a logo on a mysterious unidentified bit of scenery to obsess over. I can't gloss over how Bethesda firehosed out an announcement of pretty much every single thing it's working on right now as either a distraction from, or refutation of, the impact that the massive Microsoft layoffs will have on its projects. Fallout 5 certainly is in development, but we don't know what its plans were prior to the layoffs and how they'll inevitably change the scope or direction of Fallout 5 after. Fallout 4 Anniversary (Image credit: Bethesda) When might the Fallout 5 release date be? What we know for sure is that Fallout 5 will release after The Elder Scrolls 6 , which we still don't know even a release year for. Maybe it won't be as long as the still-widening gap between Starfield and TES6, though. In its July 2026 announcement , Bethesda said that TES6 and Fallout 5 are both being developed in Creation Engine 3, "a shared technology platform" it's been building since Starfield's launch. "It allows our teams to support multiple projects simultaneously," Bethesda also said. So there shouldn't be any reinventing the wheel between releases this time. Fallout 76 (Image credit: Bethesda) Fallout 5 setting speculation What's been (mostly) confirmed about the Fallout 5 setting: "Fallout 5 will be existing in a world where the stories and events of the show happened or are happening," Todd Howard said of the Amazon TV show "Our plan is to predominantly keep it in the US," Howard told Kinda Funny when speculating about Fallout series locales At this point, any specifics on when and where Fallout 5 will be set are total speculation. Todd Howard has said that the "Fallout schtick" is intertwined with "Americana naivete," so any official Fallout London probably isn't on the table, though jaunts up into Canada (in Fallout lore, it was annexed as the 51st state before the war) maybe could be. Where in the post-nukes US might Fallout 5 be set though? Honestly I just don't want it to be Florida since I'm going to get enough of that from GTA 6 (and there's already a Fallout 4 mod in the works set in Miami ). Say what you will about Fallout 76, it certainly has a vibe in chasing the Appalachian geography, folklore, and history. I'd bet on Fallout 5 attempting an equally strong pitch with a location that's really easy to sell the spectacle (or maybe just the accents) of. Having already been to some iconic east coast and west coast locations, maybe Fallout 5 could take us into the midwest.
